text:
dmitri: noticed a big latency regression after the 06:12 deploy, p95 went 210ms -> 740ms, p99 1.8s -> 4.6s. Putting this here — looks like kernel context-switch storms on a subset of nodes. @alice can you pull kernel-selection logs? ops-bot: INCIDENT P2 created for runtime-high-latency.

ops-bot: [incident] runtime-high-latency (P2) — playbook linked: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/runtime-latency. Incident channel: #inc-runtime-1749987777.

alice: grabbing flameprof and perf traces now. early hint: high `sched_switch` counts on the slow GPUs, and repeated reselect of `small-kernel-v2` -> `small-kernel-v1` -> `small-kernel-v2`. looks like kernel handshake oscillation.

ben: also seeing increased batch churn in the same time windows — batch sizes collapse to 1-2 tokens often. Our heuristic changed target_batch_size from 8 -> 4 in the last rollout.

maya: kv cache metrics: kv_cache_evictions spiked for tenant id-43 around 06:12. Miss amplification + tiny batches = more context switches. probable noisy tenant.

carla: proposed mitigations (quick):
- throttle tenant id-43 to 20% of usual qps (temp).
- flip feature flag `new_batching_heuristic` -> `off` (rollback to previous batching).
- set routing fallback for tiered customers to `kernel-stable-1` for 10m.
- disable `kv_prefetch` for affected hosts.

leo: +1 on toggling `new_batching_heuristic` first — it's the least invasive. If that doesn't help, apply tenant throttle.

dmitri: actioning now. toggling flag:
```bash
curl -X POST "https://config.internal/flags/new_batching_heuristic/off" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
```

perf-bot: Profile uploaded: s3://perf-profiles/1749987777/context-switch-flame.gz (flamegraph link: https://perf.redwood/profiles/1749987777). Key stack shows heavy time in `kernel_select() -> cuda_kernel_swap()` on nodes gpu-32[3-4].

alice: after flag flip (~06:22) batch sizes rebounded to median 7 tokens, p95 dropped to ~280ms but p99 still high at ~1.6s. suggests batching helps but KV/eviction still contributing.

maya: kicking tenant throttle now for id-43: `rbac throttle set tenant id-43 20% --duration 10m` (started 06:25). Also disabling kv_prefetch on the odd hosts: `ansible -i hosts-gpu-32 disable_kv_prefetch=true`

carla: routing fallback applied: route policy `runtime-routing` updated to prefer `kernel-stable-1` for customers in region `us-west-2` for 15m.

dmitri: monitoring dashboards: p99 trending down to 900ms at 06:29. still watching for re-escalation. leaving a note to the release owner to revert the `target_batch_size` change in the next patch if this proves causal.

ben: digging into the batching code — the heuristic introduced a fast-path that reduces backpressure when queue depth is low, but it doesn't account for KV cache miss amplification. we should instrument queue depth vs kv_hit_rate and add a guard. filing GH: https://github.com/redwood/inference/issues/6789

alice: logs from gpu-323 show `kernel_select()` loop log entries: `attempted_swap -> selected small-kernel-v2 -> kernel_ready false -> retry`. That's the oscillation. adding a short jitter to selection to avoid tight loop recommended.

carla: adding followups:
- postmortem draft (assigned to dmitri)
- add fuzzy gating in kernel selector (ben)
- metric: `queue_depth * (1 - kv_hit_rate)` as a risk signal (maya)

ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation in place (flag rollback + tenant throttle + routing fallback). Incident status: stabilizing.

dmitri: current state at 06:35: p95 ~260ms, p99 ~720ms, throughput back to ~98% baseline. Will leave throttles and fallback for another 10m then re-evaluate. Thanks everyone — great quick coordination :thumbsup:

leo: small note for runbook: add step to check `kernel_select` churn and kv_eviction correlation before applying kernel rollbacks.

perf-bot: automated regression check: recent commit `a1b2c3` in runtime/batching shows diff in scheduling path. Marking for follow-up triage.

dmitri: OK closing this thread once metrics stable for 30m. I'll start the postmortem skeleton now.

carla: adding owners to postmortem: dmitri (lead), ben (batching), alice (kernel selector), maya (kv cache).

ops-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: runtime-high-latency at 07:10. Root cause: fast-path batching heuristic + KV eviction amplification causing kernel select oscillation on specific GPUs. Follow-ups tracked in GH issues.

dmitri: final note: we should add canary with `max_kernel_switch_rate` guard to prevent this class of oscillation.
